input.reasoning_summary:
After investigating potential challenges to the initial verdict, all three hypotheses were either refuted or found no relevant evidence:

H1 (Restatements/Corrections): No evidence was found of any restatements, corrections, or adjustments to the reported total net sales figures. The retrieved evidence (E11, E12, E13) consistently shows the same figures of $143,756 million for Q1 2026 and $124,300 million for Q1 2025.

H2 (One-time items/Accounting changes): No evidence was found indicating that revenue growth was materially affected by one-time items, accounting changes, or non-recurring events. E14 discusses general litigation impacts but not specific to Q1 2026. E15 and E16 discuss ASU 2025-06, but this accounting standard is effective in Q1 2029 and has not been early adopted, so it did not affect the Q1 2026 results.

H3 (Different quarter lengths): This challenge is REFUTED. Evidence E17, E18, and E19 all confirm that fiscal years 2025 and 2024 both spanned 52 weeks each, ensuring comparability between the quarters. The 53-week year occurred in fiscal 2023, not in the periods being compared.

The original verdict remains SUPPORTED. The evidence clearly shows total net sales of $143,756 million for the quarter ended December 27, 2025 compared to $124,300 million for the quarter ended December 28, 2024, representing a 16% year-over-year increase, which exceeds the claimed threshold of 15%.
